automatic_writers.note: Writers that are part of the product. A lane controller or a supervised guard joins this list when its design ships. config_sources names a writer by config_audit.source when its actor also writes by hand: metal-box-stop-loop is the box stop loop, which runs as the systemd unit virev-box-stop.service since Crawler VP p173 closed on 10-16 00:40Z, while actor metal also writes by hand from source metal-owner. canary-roster is the engage canary roster refill (crawler-v3 canary_roster.py), which keeps the roster at the owner's 10% of active accounts. hold-expiry is the rate-controller role writing a guard switch such as supply_hold.enabled back on when the end its hand switch-off carried has come (crawler-v3 hold_expiry.py, F18). rate-controller is the prod lane rate controller, F1's design, which made 544 of the 588 F1 rows in the 24 h to 10-19 15:40Z after the Crawler VP closed p170 at 15:15Z. contact-refresh is the crawler's contact refresh dropping a stored discovered email point whose own page its run refused (crawler-v3 contacts/service.py refused_points, F34's design 522040a336), one contact_points.retract row per refresh.

exempt.config_reason_regex: ^owner: "|A/B|live-ab W\d|^Owner order|the owner's order of \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}: '|owner (?:ruling|rule) on (?:todo )?t\d+|^Owner's [^(]{0,60}\(todo t\d+|\bowner t\d+\b
exempt.note: An owner order quoted in the reason or opened with 'Owner order', or a named A/B experiment with its restore, is a decision, not a hand fix, and so is the restore row of a named live-ab window (audit 14869, proxy.connect_racers back to 20 after live-ab W1 on 10-19). The staging `.venv/bin/python - 3600 8` exec and the prod `python -c "$0"` exec of the script that opens 'Daily B2 version inventory for ONE bucket' are the declared unit virev-b2-inventory.service (host.yml --tags b2-inventory, its timer; on prod run-inventory.sh calls inventory.py host influencer-prod virev-prod-crawler-worker, read 10-18 05:34Z), so neither is a hand-started process. A board note on a d3 run or the d3 precheck reports this duty's own work, not a hand fix. A reason that quotes the owner's dated order (the owner's order of 2026-10-13: 'can we not enrich for now?', pause.enrich audit 14089) is the same kind of decision, and so is a reason that cites the owner's answer on a For you todo by id ('owner ruling on todo t61', 'owner rule on t65', 'Owner's fixed census cap (todo t67, c170)', audits 16761, 16777 and 16768 on 10-26). A key named in config_key_regex is a lane's fixed cap that owner rule c170 (10-26) has operators set by hand from measured good reads, so a change that writes only such keys is design, not a hand fix. meta_ads.walker_sessions_max is the one operator cap a climb knob reads (crawler-v3 control/climb.py top_key); prod audit 16886 set it to 360 on 10-28 03:51Z and read as F1. A write to meta_ads.walker_sessions itself still counts as F1. lanes.max_processes.<role> is the operator ceiling of one elastic crawler lane (crawler-v3 run/lane_scale.py rule 10), the same kind of c170 cap: on 10-28 audit 16879 set meta-ads-writer to 12 from measured reads (about 62 pages/s at 93 ms against 44-50 at 307 ms with 24), and audits 16881 and 16888 set the census writer to 18 and back. They were trimmed because prod Postgres was full at 600, and the crawler now keeps itself under the line with no ceiling: the lane scaler counts its container at full pools against the live max_connections (auto-sns-agent 512b5eeb5), the boot gate closes its connection (eb3de1d4c), and test_prod_full_pools_fit_the_pg_budget holds the lane floors under that line (bd44cfd37; design 01a11bd7-072f-7591-ad1d-f123c276cde5/p244). A reason that names the owner's answer on a todo as 'owner t<n>', the form crawler-v3 control/hold_expiry.py OWNER_ORDER reads as an owner's order, is the same decision: prod audit 16839 (instagram_census.history_years 20 -> 3, 10-27 07:58Z) cites 'owner t74', the owner's answer '3 years' on the Crawler VP's todo t74, and read as an F1 repeat because only the 'owner rule on t<n>' form matched. declared_cap_regex names the lane caps whose value is committed in crawler-v3: a write to one of them is design when its value equals that key's default in settings.py (_PROD_CONTROL_DEFAULTS or _STAGING_CONTROL_DEFAULTS, with the constants control/tuning.py sets) at the newest commit before the write on any dev branch (gitDeclaredCaps), so an operator commits the cap with its reading and may then write that value at once (c100) instead of waiting for the release; any other value is a hand step of F31.
